title: Pluggable extraction / classification / merge endpoint (OpenAI-compatible local chat)
background: Extraction is the BIGGEST leak: turning a document into articles sends its FULL CONTENT to Anthropic, and the endpoint is hardcoded at lib/loopctl/llm/anthropic.ex:37 (@base_url, used at :139) with no env var and no tenant field. There is no provider behaviour. However, six TASK-level behaviours already exist and every one is config-swappable (all are Mox-mapped in config/test.exs:312,378,395): Knowledge.ExtractorBehaviour (llm_extractor.ex:20), Knowledge.ClassifierBehaviour (claude_category_classifier.ex:17), Knowledge.MergeSynthesizerBehaviour (claude_merge_synthesizer.ex:14), Knowledge.ContentExtractorBehaviour (claude_content_extractor.ex:18), Memory.Promoter.LlmBehaviour (promoter/default_llm.ex), Knowledge.EmbeddingBehaviour (embedding_client.ex:31, resolved at knowledge.ex:8110). Each current impl calls Loopctl.Llm.Anthropic directly. The 2026-07-15 draft deferred this story as 'bigger scope'; that assessment was wrong - the seam already exists, so this is a set of sibling modules, not a refactor of the LLM layer. Note also that the chat-endpoint write surface (set_llm_config) is role :user for the same reason as US-41.2: the PATCH carries tenant secrets.

story.as_a: an agent harvesting a user's private documents
story.i_want_to: have extraction, classification and merge run against a local OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint instead of Anthropic
story.so_that: the document's full text - the largest and most sensitive payload in the pipeline - never leaves the tenant's chosen boundary

rationale: Closing embeddings (US-41.2) while leaving extraction on a hardcoded vendor endpoint would ship a privacy tier that leaks the actual documents. Extraction is where the raw content goes, so a private tier without it is worse than none - it would be a guarantee that is false in the one place users most assume it holds.

acceptance_criteria.description: An OpenAI-compatible chat client module exists alongside Loopctl.Llm.Anthropic, taking base_url + key + model from tenant settings, with the same return contract and the same ProviderError mapping (llm/provider_error.ex) so callers are unchanged.

Sibling implementations of the four content behaviours (extractor, classifier, merge synthesizer, content extractor) plus the memory promoter LLM route to the OpenAI-compatible client. Selection is per-tenant at runtime, NOT a compile-time config swap, because two tenants on one node may use different providers - AND the existing DI seam is PRESERVED rather than replaced: the module named in config stays the single resolution point (Application.get_env, per CLAUDE.md's config-based DI) and BECOMES A TENANT-AWARE ROUTER that dispatches to the Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible sibling based on tenant settings. config/test.exs's Mox mappings are therefore untouched; no test uses Application.put_env and no dependency is passed as a function opt. A test asserts two tenants resolve different siblings through the same configured module on one node.

Endpoint, model and provider for the chat surface are settable through the EXISTING set_llm_config MCP tool + matching API, consistent with US-41.2, and carry the same config-time probe and remediation shape (a trivial completion is issued before persisting). Like US-41.2 AC-41.2.2 that write stays ROLE :user - the epic's agent-manageability audit is corrected to user-write for this row, since the same PATCH stores tenant secrets and CLAUDE.md's role checklist forbids downgrading it to :agent. The probe consults the single egress policy module (US-41.4 AC-41.4.9), not a private URL policy - which is why this story DEPENDS on US-41.4 and is implemented after it. It also carries US-41.2 AC-41.2.3's credential rule verbatim: changing the chat endpoint requires a matching key in the same PATCH or an explicit acknowledgement that the stored key will be transmitted to the new host; the probe never ships an existing credential to a new host silently.

Local models are weaker at structured output than Claude: every impl validates the response shape and fails the item with a legible, agent-readable reason rather than writing malformed articles. A model that cannot produce the required structure is reported as a configuration problem, not silently degraded output.

Every provider call from the new client passes through Provider.Admission (as anthropic.ex:118 does) so backpressure and the US-41.4 egress guard apply uniformly. Adding the provider is TWO coordinated edits, not one: the new atom joins the fixed @providers list (never a user-supplied value, never String.to_atom on input) AND a matching limit_for/1 clause plus a @default_<provider>_rpm and a provider_admission_<name>_rpm SystemConfig key are added (admission.ex:104,194-201). Without the limit clause the call raises FunctionClauseError inside the try body and admission.ex:145's rescue converts it to fail_open -> :ok, i.e. a provider with NO rate limit at exactly the call site the US-41.4 guard must sit beside. A unit test asserts the new provider is actually rate-limited and NOT fail-opened. The single shared atom for all tenant-supplied local endpoints means one global RPM ceiling across tenants with different hardware; that is INTENTIONAL for v1 (bucket keys isolate counts, the limit is shared) and is documented as such.

Token usage / cost accounting continues to work for the alternate provider, or the story explicitly records that a local endpoint reports no usage and how that is represented (a zero-cost provider is fine; a silently missing usage row is not).
Default unchanged: a tenant that configures nothing keeps Anthropic with the hardcoded endpoint and identical behavior.

test_cases.name: tenant-scoped provider selection through the unchanged DI seam
preconditions: tenant B configured to a stub OpenAI-compatible endpoint
steps: run an extraction for each tenant in the same node
expected_results: A hits Anthropic, B hits the stub
both resolve through the module named in config - the Mox mapping in config/test.exs still intercepts
no cross-contamination of client or credentials

test_cases.name: malformed local-model output fails legibly
preconditions: stub endpoint returning prose instead of the required structure
expected_results: item fails with a shape-validation reason naming the endpoint and model

test_cases.name: admission applies to the new provider and does not fail open
preconditions: admission limit exhausted for the new provider
steps: separately, call with the limit resolution path exercised
expected_results: no FunctionClauseError reaches the rescue/fail_open path - limit_for/1 has a clause for the new provider

test_cases.name: usage accounting present for the alternate provider
expected_results: a usage record exists with the documented representation - never a silently absent row

technical_notes: Do NOT introduce a grand provider abstraction over Anthropic + OpenAI. The task-level behaviours are the existing, tested seam; adding sibling impls keeps the blast radius small and the review tractable.

Anthropic's messages API and the OpenAI chat-completions API differ in system-prompt handling and tool/JSON-mode semantics - the differences belong INSIDE the new client, so the behaviour contract stays identical.

config/test.exs already maps all these behaviours to Mox mocks; the tenant-aware router keeps that mapping the seam config/test.exs points at (Knowledge.ExtractorBehaviour -> MockExtractor etc.), so no test needs Application.put_env (CLAUDE.md forbids it) and no existing test changes.

Per-tenant runtime selection means the ROUTER's functions take tenant_id and resolve the sibling per call - resist the temptation to reuse the compile-time Application.compile_env pattern used by Oban workers here. This is a deliberate, documented departure from the compile-time half of the config-based DI convention, and the reason is that provider choice is tenant data, not deployment config.
